findings.highlight: I remove the nerve I gouged into my spine.
findings.evidenceJa: 背骨に抉り込んだ感覚を外す。
findings.governingReading: Shirou disengages the sensation embedded in his spine, after which circuit-related tension releases.
findings.explanation: Releasing a sensation becomes removing a nerve. The English makes the description more concrete, though the magical context does not require literal anatomical extraction.

findings.highlight: Saber actually seems to ruefully mutter something under her breath
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーはまったくです、なんて珍しく軽口を言って
findings.governingReading: Saber answers his double-Fuji-nee joke with the unusually casual quip “Exactly,” then sits beside him.
findings.explanation: Saber’s rare lighthearted agreement with Shirou disappears into an unspecified rueful mutter.

findings.highlight: He was often spacey and a klutz.
findings.evidenceJa: 普段はぼーっとしていて、どうも冴えなかった。
findings.governingReading: Shirou fondly recalls Kiritsugu as habitually vague and somehow lacking in sharpness or distinction.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu being absent-minded and unimpressive becomes being a klutz.

findings.highlight: you need to enjoy life to its fullest
findings.evidenceJa: 楽しむ時は思いっきり楽しむんだ
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu would say that when it was time to have fun, one should enjoy it wholeheartedly, and then romp like a child.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu’s maxim about fully enjoying occasions of enjoyment becomes a general injunction to enjoy life to the fullest.

findings.highlight: that might've genuinely been the most fun time in my life.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分にとって純粋に楽しい時間だったのかもしれない。
findings.governingReading: Looking back, Shirou thinks those five years may have been a time he could enjoy without admixture or reservation.
findings.explanation: A possibly purely enjoyable five-year period becomes the most enjoyable time in Shirou’s entire life.

findings.highlight: that clown was immature as well
findings.evidenceJa: そいつも子供のような人物だった
findings.governingReading: Saber unexpectedly refers to her former magus with the rough but nonspecific そいつ, prompting Shirou to notice the lapse in her usual decorum.
findings.explanation: Saber’s deliberately casual “that fellow” becomes the stronger insult “that clown.”

findings.highlight: He sounds like trouble, for sure.
findings.evidenceJa: まるで希代の悪人みたいじゃないか
findings.governingReading: Startled by her phrasing, Shirou jokes that she makes him sound like a villain without equal.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s hyperbole that Saber makes the man sound like an unparalleled villain is reduced to ordinary trouble.

findings.highlight: I am sure he is still somewhere speaking on the topic.
findings.evidenceJa: きっと、今でも呑気に愛を語っているのでしょう
findings.governingReading: Despite his imprisonment, Saber imagines that he is probably still blithely speaking of love even now.
findings.explanation: Saber’s imagined picture of the old man still carefree and talking about love loses both the love and the carefree manner.

findings.highlight: seems to swallow back on saying more.
findings.evidenceJa: ほんの少しだけ言葉を呑んだ。
findings.governingReading: After the reminiscence, Saber checks herself or leaves a slight portion unsaid.
findings.explanation: The narration of Saber briefly swallowing her words is rendered with the malformed construction “swallow back on saying more.”

findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの敵意は殺気に変わりつつある。
findings.governingReading: As Archer advances, her hostility begins to sharpen into palpable lethal intent.
findings.explanation: Saber’s hostility turning into killing intent becomes merely turning violent.

findings.highlight: your movements are seven centimeters off from your center
findings.evidenceJa: 動作が中よりに七センチほどずれている
findings.governingReading: The numb side’s movements are shifted roughly seven centimeters toward the inside relative to where Shirou intends them.
findings.explanation: Archer’s diagnosis of movements displaced about seven centimeters inward is recast as displacement from Shirou’s center.

findings.highlight: Since you don't know what you're doing, the circuit that is supposed to be used has been neglected and is dormant.
findings.evidenceJa: そのような勘違いをしているから、本来使われる筈の回路が放棄され、眠っていたのだ。
findings.governingReading: Because Shirou mistakenly treats circuits as something made each time, the circuits meant for use were abandoned and left dormant.
findings.explanation: Archer’s specific causal accusation about Shirou’s misconception becomes the broader insult that he does not know what he is doing.

findings.highlight: The nerves will eventually recall its normal function
findings.evidenceJa: いずれ神経は通常の機能を思い出す
findings.governingReading: The nerves will eventually remember their normal function as the dormant circuit returns to service.
findings.explanation: The explanation mismatches plural “nerves” with singular “its.”

findings.highlight: The needle stabs my back again.
findings.evidenceJa: もう一度、背中に鍼が刺さる。
findings.governingReading: The earlier sensation likened to a needle returns a second time when Archer touches his back; no physical needle has been introduced.
findings.explanation: The renewed needle-like pain is turned into a literal needle stabbing Shirou’s back.

findings.highlight: I also had one of my arms taken away when I did it for the first time.
findings.evidenceJa: 私も初めは片腕をもっていかれた。
findings.governingReading: Archer says that at first an arm was “taken” from him, a phrase that can describe losing the arm’s use or suffering severe damage without settling the exact event here.
findings.explanation: Archer’s compressed claim that the same process once cost him an arm is made into an apparently literal removal of the limb.

findings.highlight: It is nothing worth mentioning. The reason I fight is simply for myself.
findings.evidenceJa: 知れた事。私の戦う意義は、ただ己の為のみだ。
findings.governingReading: Asked what he fights for, Archer answers that it is self-evident: he fights solely for himself.
findings.explanation: Archer’s “the answer is obvious” becomes “it is nothing worth mentioning.”

findings.highlight: The only things that save a person are their own will and results.
findings.evidenceJa: 人を叶えるのは本人の意思と結果だけだ。
findings.governingReading: Outside salvation is not true salvation; only the person’s own will and its result can bring that person to fulfillment or realization.
findings.explanation: Archer’s distinction between outside rescue and a person being realized through their own will and result is flattened into another statement about saving.
